methods.label: Semicircle and corner sector
methods.explanation:
The rope sweeps a semicircle outside the wall where it is attached. Additional roaming area is possible only if some rope remains after reaching a corner.

In arrangement I, the attachment is \(8\) feet from both corners. The \(8\)-foot rope can just reach either corner, leaving no length to extend around it. Thus the roaming area is
\[
A_{\mathrm{I}}=\frac12\pi(8)^2=32\pi.
\]
In arrangement II, the attachment is \(4\) feet from the upper corner and \(16-4=12\) feet from the lower corner. The dog can reach only the upper corner. After the rope bends around that corner, \(8-4=4\) feet remain, allowing an additional quarter-circle above the shed, beyond the line containing the attachment wall. This new region has no interior overlap with the original semicircle. The rope cannot reach another corner because each shed side is \(16\) feet long.

Therefore
\[
A_{\mathrm{II}}=32\pi+\frac14\pi(4)^2=36\pi.
\]
Arrangement II gives \(36\pi-32\pi=4\pi\) more square feet, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
